scenario.title: Entering through a terminal or an agent
situations: A human runs the installer in a terminal
A human tells an existing agent: install upyoke.com
Installation stops halfway or changes presentation mode
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: Can an agent with no Yoke-specific context complete the exact public entry path?
Does every failure preserve enough context to resume without guessing?

lessons.title: Finding Yoke before Yoke is installed
lessons.need: The terminal user needs the visible install command. An existing agent needs public instructions before any Yoke hook, skill or packet is available.
lessons.surface: Public install page; proposed homepage agent entry
lessons.gap: FIRST-USER B plans the homepage route. The complete first-turn fetch → correct install action still needs real-agent proof.

lessons.title: One setup decision at a time
lessons.need: The TUI teaches the human directly. Agent mode must provide a structured question, allowed answers, links and guidance, which the agent translates for the human.
lessons.surface: Current TUI/noninteractive setup; FIRST-USER A structured agent steps
lessons.gap: The audited adapter does not yet expose the planned --agent / --answer contract. A noninteractive flag alone is not the proposed context chain.

lessons.title: Authentication, progress and a recoverable finish
lessons.when: Browser authorization, Apply, failure and completion
lessons.need: Show what changed, what is waiting for the human, and one continuation. TUI browser actions and agent-returned links/codes are different channels.
lessons.surface: Setup screens, step results and resume handoff
lessons.gap: Trace expiration, denial, partial Apply, Back and mode switching. Preserve original intent, project and run identity. A checkout linked to another install's project offers Unlink and set up fresh before Apply.
